run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T10:22:55Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because frontend-proxy's own ingress spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and the alert's condition is error rate above zero. Over the authorized window (09:22:55-10:30:32Z) the span metric shows 31.48 error 'ingress' spans against 22,490 ingress spans with no status (about 0.14%), while its client-side 'router frontend egress' spans show 0 errors. The 31 error requests appear in the frontend-proxy access log as HTTP 503 with response flag UC and response-code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} towards upstream cluster 'frontend' (upstream host 100.70.94.93:8080, the frontend ClusterIP): the connection to the frontend upstream was terminated before a response started. The observed failures run from 09:56:09Z to 10:26:37Z at roughly one per minute, so the alert reflects a small sustained trickle rather than a spike. Nothing further downstream is shown to be failing: the frontend service records zero error spans on all of its operations, including its gRPC client calls to product-catalog, cart, checkout, ad, recommendation and shipping, and both frontend and frontend-proxy pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts since 09:43Z and memory well under their limits. Why the frontend closes those connections cannot be established from the available telemetry: the frontend container emitted no log lines, Jaeger holds no traces after 09:55:50Z (so none of the reset requests is covered by a trace), and the RequestErrorRate rule expression is not retrievable from Prometheus. CPU pressure is real but unproven as a cause: frontend is limited to 100m CPU and was CFS-throttled in about 29% of its periods, yet the error spans' p99 (938 ms) is shorter than that of successful ingress spans (1302 ms), which argues against a timeout-driven explanation.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's span metrics in the window record 31.484375 error spans on operation 'ingress' (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) and 0 error spans on operation 'router frontend egress', against 22490 'ingress' spans with STATUS_CODE_UNSET; roughly 0.14% of its ingress spans are errors.

frontend-proxy access logs show 31 non-2xx responses between 09:56:09Z and 10:26:37Z, all of them '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with upstream cluster 'frontend' and upstream host 100.70.94.93:8080; no 500, 502, 504 or 429 responses appear in the read log slices.
The upstream host 100.70.94.93:8080 named in those 503 log lines is the ClusterIP:8080 of the Kubernetes Service 'frontend' in namespace otel-demo (selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend).

The errors are sustained and low-rate rather than a spike: the 120s-resolution error series shows 0 to about 2.67 error ingress spans per 2 minutes at intervals scattered across the window (e.g. 0 at 09:56:55Z, 2.67 at 09:58:55Z, 1.33 at 10:20:55Z, 2.67 at 10:22:55Z, 0 at 10:28:55Z).

Across all services, the only STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counts in the window are frontend-proxy 'ingress' 31.48, recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 4.06, ad 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 2.04 and fraud-detection 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 2.04; every frontend operation, including all of its gRPC client spans, has 0 error spans.

The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh (IP 100.96.2.139, node i-030aedeb6471c8a81) and the frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt (IP 100.96.2.218) are both Running, ready, restartCount 0 with no lastState termination recorded and container start times of 09:43:04Z.

All 21 pods in namespace otel-demo report startTime between 09:42:59Z and 09:44:52Z with restart counts of 0 (fraud-detection has 1), i.e. the environment was created shortly before the errors began and no pod restarted during the incident window.

Resource settings and pressure: the frontend container has limits cpu=100m / memory=200Mi and the frontend-proxy container cpu=30m / memory=50Mi; over the window the frontend container was CFS-throttled in 0.291 of its periods and frontend-proxy in 0.057, while max working set was 129,208,320 bytes for frontend and 21,123,072 bytes for frontend-proxy.
Ingress p99 duration over the window was 1302.72 ms for STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans and 938.00 ms for STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, so the erroring requests were not the slowest ones.

The trace evidence available for frontend-proxy was already stale and truncated when captured: the kept traces_search slice has data_as_of 2026-11-15T09:55:50.007135Z (freshness 2086 s), is incomplete with 600 of 640 rows omitted, and every frontend-proxy span in its first 40 rows carries http.status_code 200 with no error tags.

The 503s originate at the frontend HTTP server: frontend-proxy's requests reached the frontend upstream and the peer closed the connection before the response started (UC / upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}), the usual shape of an upstream closing a pooled keep-alive connection as a request is dispatched on it. The mechanism is not verifiable here because the frontend container produced no log lines and no trace exists for any of the reset requests.

Frontend CPU starvation (100m limit, 0.291 CFS throttling ratio) may contribute to how the frontend handles its sockets and could raise the frequency of prematurely terminated connections, but this is unproven and weakened by the fact that error spans are no slower than successful ones (938 ms vs 1302 ms p99), which does not fit a response-timeout pattern.

The alert's reported value 0.0333 may be an error rate per second over a short evaluation window rather than a request ratio, since the measured span ratio over the whole hour is about 0.0014; the alerting rule expression could not be read, so this remains unverified.

A pod restart, crash or OOM on frontend or frontend-proxy is not supported: both containers are ready with restartCount 0, no lastState.terminated is recorded, and frontend memory working set peaked at about 129 MB against a 200 MiB limit.

A failing dependency inside the frontend is not supported: the frontend service shows 0 error spans on all its operations, including grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (19386 spans), CartService/GetCart (5331), CartService/AddItem (3521), CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (1161), AdService/GetAds (1887) and RecommendationService/ListRecommendations (1876), all with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and none with STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

The flagd EventStream error spans on ad (2.04), fraud-detection (2.04) and recommendation (4.06) are not attributable to frontend-proxy's ingress errors: they are separate streaming spans on other services, and no evidence in this run ties them to the 503s towards the frontend upstream.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for rule_name=RequestErrorRate, for {severity="warning"} or for the unfiltered query (all status no_data), so the expression, threshold, window and 'for' duration behind the reported value 0.0333 are unknown.

Whether frontend-proxy logged any non-2xx response before 09:56:09Z is unknown: the query covering 09:43:05Z-09:56:09Z hit the 4 MiB log read limit and returned status no_data (1681 lines removed by the exclude filter, read cut at 10:13:57Z), so the earlier interval could not be examined as evidence.

The frontend container produced no log lines at all in the window (fetch_pod_logs read 0 bytes for container 'frontend', status no_data), so the frontend application's own view of the terminated connections, its HTTP keep-alive settings and any server-side errors are unknown.

Jaeger has no trace data after 2026-11-15T09:55:50Z: traces_search for frontend-proxy in 10:20:00-10:26:00Z and traces_search_by_tags with error=true and otel.status_code=ERROR both returned no_data, so none of the 31 reset requests is covered by a span and no error details or parent-child chain can be inspected for them.
No Kubernetes events were returned for namespace otel-demo inside the window (two event queries, status no_data), so probe failures, evictions or controller events during the incident are unknown.

kube-state-metrics series (kube_*) and any http_*/rpc_*/app_* series are absent from this Prometheus (both name and label lookups returned no_data), so deployment/pod readiness history and HTTP or gRPC server-side error metrics are unknown rather than zero.

The otel-collector container also produced no log lines in the window (status no_data), so a collector-side pipeline problem cannot be checked; the observed stop of trace export to Jaeger at about 09:55:50Z remains unexplained.

Change history is not an integrated source for this run, so what caused all otel-demo pods to start at about 09:43Z and whether anything changed at about 09:56Z, when the first observed 503 appears, could not be verified.

No impact on callers other than frontend-proxy's own ingress responses was observed, and downstream or customer impact is unverified; confirming it would require caller-side error metrics that this Prometheus does not expose.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition (expression, rate window, threshold and 'for') from the alerting configuration to confirm exactly which signal and window the 0.0333 value comes from.

Inspect frontend application logging and compare the frontend HTTP server's keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout with the Envoy upstream idle timeout and retry settings for the 'frontend' cluster in frontend-proxy; if this is a keep-alive close race, aligning those timeouts or retrying 503/UC on the frontend route would remove the spurious 503s.

Investigate why Jaeger holds no traces after 09:55:50Z (collector traces exporter or queue) so the affected requests can be traced end to end, and re-run the pre-09:56Z frontend-proxy log query with a later start_time to get under the 4 MiB read limit.

If HTTP latency matters, review the frontend container's 100m CPU limit given the about 29% CFS throttling observed, and the frontend-proxy 30m limit, as a capacity follow-up independent of the alert threshold.
